title: שמות פרק 29
english: And this is the thing that thou shalt do unto them to hallow them, to minister unto me in the priest's office: Take one young bullock, and two rams without blemish,
And unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened tempered with oil, and wafers unleavened anointed with oil: of wheaten flour shalt thou make them.
And thou shalt put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, with the bullock and the two rams.
And Aaron and his sons thou shalt bring unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and shalt wash them with water.
And thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the coat, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him with the curious girdle of the ephod:
And thou shalt put the mitre upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the mitre.
Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his head, and anoint him.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.
And thou shalt gird them with girdles, Aaron and his sons, and put the bonnets on them: and the priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.
And thou shalt cause a bullock to be brought before the tabernacle of the congregation: and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the bullock.
And thou shalt kill the bullock before the Lord, by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock, and put it upon the horns of the altar with thy finger, and pour all the blood beside the bottom of the altar.
And thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul that is above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and burn them upon the altar.
But the flesh of the bullock, and his skin, and his dung, shalt thou burn with fire without the camp: it is a sin offering.
Thou shalt also take one ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.
And thou shalt slay the ram, and thou shalt take his blood, and sprinkle it round about upon the altar.
And thou shalt cut the ram in pieces, and wash the inwards of him, and his legs, and put them unto his pieces, and unto his head.
And thou shalt burn the whole ram upon the altar: it is a burnt offering unto the Lord: it is a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram.

Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.

And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons with him: and he shall be hallowed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons' garments with him.

Also thou shalt take of the ram the fat and the rump, and the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder; for it is a ram of consecration:
And one loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer out of the basket of the unleavened bread that is before the Lord:
And thou shalt put all in the hands of Aaron, and in the hands of his sons; and shalt wave them for a wave offering before the Lord.
And thou shalt receive them of their hands, and burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour before the Lord: it is an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
And thou shalt take the breast of the ram of Aaron's consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before the Lord: and it shall be thy part.

And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons:

And it shall be Aaron's and his sons' by a statute for ever from the children of Israel: for it is an heave offering: and it shall be an heave offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifice of their peace offerings, even their heave offering unto the Lord.
And the holy garments of Aaron shall be his sons' after him, to be anointed therein, and to be consecrated in them.
And that son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days, when he cometh into the tabernacle of the congregation to minister in the holy place.
And thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and seethe his flesh in the holy place.
And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket by the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And they shall eat those things wherewith the atonement was made, to consecrate and to sanctify them: but a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy.
And if ought of the flesh of the consecrations, or of the bread, remain unto the morning, then thou shalt burn the remainder with fire: it shall not be eaten, because it is holy.
And thus shalt thou do unto Aaron, and to his sons, according to all things which I have commanded thee: seven days shalt thou consecrate them.
And thou shalt offer every day a bullock for a sin offering for atonement: and thou shalt cleanse the altar, when thou hast made an atonement for it, and thou shalt anoint it, to sanctify it.
Seven days thou shalt make an atonement for the altar, and sanctify it; and it shall be an altar most holy: whatsoever toucheth the altar shall be holy.
Now this is that which thou shalt offer upon the altar; two lambs of the first year day by day continually.
The one lamb thou shalt offer in the morning; and the other lamb thou shalt offer at even:
And with the one lamb a tenth deal of flour mingled with the fourth part of an hin of beaten oil; and the fourth part of an hin of wine for a drink offering.

And the other lamb thou shalt offer at even, and shalt do thereto according to the meat offering of the morning, and according to the drink offering thereof, for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
This shall be a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the Lord: where I will meet you, to speak there unto thee.
And there I will meet with the children of Israel, and the tabernacle shall be sanctified by my glory.
And I will sanctify the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar: I will sanctify also both Aaron and his sons, to minister to me in the priest's office.
And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, that brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, that I may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God.
ai_explanation: הציווי נאמר לאהרן ולבניו, כדי לקדש אותם לכהונה. יש לקחת פר אחד, שהוא בשנתו השלישית, ושני אילים; כולם צריכים להיות שלמים וללא מום.
יש להכין כמה סוגים של מאפים שלא החמיצו: לחם, חלות מצות ורקיקי מצות. את המאפים מכינים מסולת חיטים, והם עשויים בצורות שונות, עם מים רותחים או שמן, או במשיחה בשמן.
יש להניח את כל המאפים בסל אחד ולהקריב אותם יחד עם הפר ושני האילים. בהמשך מוסבר מה לעשות בכל אחד מהפריטים.
יש להביא את אהרן ואת בניו אל פתח אוהל מועד ולטבול אותם במים.
יש להלביש את אהרן בכותונת, ומעליה במעיל האפוד, באפוד ובחושן. לאחר מכן יש לחגור אותו בחשב האפוד.
יש לשים את המצנפת על ראש אהרן, ואת נזר הקודש, כלומר הציץ, על המצנפת.
יש לצקת את שמן המשחה על ראש אהרן ולמשוח אותו. את השמן יוצקים על הראש ולא על המצנפת.
יש להביא את בני אהרן ולהלביש אותם כותנות.

יש לחגור באבנט גם את אהרן וגם את בניו; אצל אהרן כבר הוזכר קודם חגור נוסף, בחשב האפוד. יש לחבוש לבני אהרן מגבעות, והלבשת הכוהנים ומשיחתם מקדשות את הכהונה לדורות לכל צאצאיהם; מילוי ידי אהרן ובניו ממנה אותם לכהונה.
יש להביא את הפר לפני אוהל מועד. אהרן ובניו צריכים להישען בכוח בידיהם על ראש הפר, בין קרניו.
יש לשחוט את הפר לפני ה', בפתח אוהל מועד.
יש לקחת מדם הפר ולתת אותו באצבע על כל אחת מקרנות המזבח הגדול שבחצר המשכן. את שאר הדם שבכלי יש לשפוך אל יסוד המזבח.
יש לקחת את כל השומן המכסה את האיברים הפנימיים, את הסרעפת הסמוכה לכבד, את שתי הכליות ואת השומן שעליהן, ולשרוף אותם על המזבח עד שיעלו עשן. חלקים אלה נקראים בלשון חכמים "אימורים".
יש לשרוף מחוץ למחנה את בשר הפר, את עורו ואת הפרש שבו. זהו קרבן חטאת שדמו ניתן על המזבח החיצון, אך בשרו אינו נאכל, וכל חלקיו שאינם מוקטרים נשרפים מחוץ למחנה.
יש לקחת את האיל האחד, ואהרן ובניו צריכים לסמוך את ידיהם על ראש האיל.
יש לשחוט את האיל, לאסוף את דמו במזרק ולזרוק אותו על זוויות המזבח, כך שיגיע לכל סביבותיו. כאן הדם אינו נמרח באצבע כמו בקרבן חטאת.
יש לנתח את האיל לחלקים, לרחוץ את חלקיו הפנימיים ואת רגליו, ולהניח אותם יחד עם הנתחים ועם ראשו, שנחתך קודם לכן.
יש להקטיר את כל האיל על המזבח, מפני שקרבן עולה עולה כולו לה'. זהו קרבן אש לה', וריחו ריח נעים הגורם נחת רוח.
יש לקחת את האיל השני, ואהרן ובניו צריכים לסמוך את ידיהם על ראש האיל.

יש לשחוט את האיל ולשים מדמו על התנוך של אוזן אהרן ושל אוזני בניו הימניות, על בוהן ידם הימנית ועל בוהן רגלם הימנית. לאחר מכן יש לזרוק על המזבח את הדם שנשאר בכלי; אין ודאות מהו בדיוק התנוך, וחכמים נחלקו בזיהויו.
יש לקחת מן הדם שעל המזבח ומן השמן של שמן המשחה, ולהזות אותם על אהרן, על בגדיו, על בניו ועל בגדיהם. כך הם ובגדיהם מתקדשים.
יש לקחת מן האיל את החלב, את האליה שהיא זנב מעובה בשומן, את החלב המכסה את הקרב, את יותרת הכבד, את שתי הכליות ואת החלב שעליהן, וכן את השוק הימנית. זהו איל המילואים, הקרבן החד־פעמי של מינוי הכוהנים.
יש לקחת כיכר לחם אחת, חלת לחם שמן אחת ורקיק אחד מתוך סל המצות שנמצא לפני ה'. הכיכר נלקחת מלחם המצות, והחלה מתוך החלות הבלולות בשמן.
יש לשים את חלקי הקרבן ואת המצות על כפות ידיהם של אהרן ובניו, ולהרים את ידיהם המלאות בתנופה לפני ה'.
יש לקחת את חלקי האיל ואת תרומת המצות מידי הכוהנים ולהקטיר אותם על המזבח, בנוסף לאיל הראשון. הקטרה זו היא קרבן אש לה', לריח ניחוח לפניו.
יש לקחת את החזה מאיל המילואים של אהרן, להניף אותו לפני ה', והוא יהיה מנה למשה. קרבן זה הוא קרבן שלמים.
יש להפריש את חזה התנופה ואת שוק התרומה מאיל המילואים. בקרבן המילואים החזה ניתן למשה והשוק הוקטרה על המזבח, אך בדרך כלל החזה והשוק שייכים לכוהנים בכל קרבנות השלמים.
החזה והשוק יהיו מעתה ולתמיד לאהרן ולבניו מאת בני ישראל. הם מופרשים מקרבנות השלמים, ונתינתם לכוהנים נחשבת תרומה לה'.
בגדי הקודש של אהרן יעברו לבניו אחריו, כדי להתגדל בהם ולהתמנות באמצעותם לתפקידם.
הכוהן הגדול שיבוא במקום אהרן יצטרך ללבוש את בגדי הכוהן הגדול במשך שבעה ימים לפני שיבוא אל אוהל מועד לשרת בקודש, כהכנה לשירותו.
יש לקחת את איל המילואים ולבשל את בשרו במקום קדוש, כלומר בחצר אוהל מועד.
אהרן ובניו יאכלו את בשר האיל ואת הלחם שנשאר בסל בפתח אוהל מועד. כאן הכוהנים נחשבים לבעלי קרבן השלמים, ולכן הם אוכלים אותו.
הכוהנים יאכלו את חלקי הקרבנות שבאמצעותם כופרו והוקדשו. זר לא יאכל מהם, מפני שהם קודש.
אם יישאר עד הבוקר מבשר המילואים או מהלחם שהכוהנים אוכלים, יש לשרוף את הנותר באש, מפני שאסור לאוכלו והוא קודש.
משה יעשה לאהרן ולבניו את כל מה שנצטווה לעשות, ובמשך שבעה ימים ימלא את ידם לתפקידם.
בכל אחד משבעת ימי המילואים יש להביא את פר החטאת לשם כפרה, ולטהר את המזבח באמצעות דם הפר הניתן עליו. לאחר מכן יש למשוח את המזבח כדי לקדשו.
במשך שבעה ימים מכפרים על המזבח ומקדשים אותו, ולאחר מכן הוא נעשה קודש קודשים, כלומר קדוש מאוד. כל דבר הראוי לקרבן שנוגע במזבח ונמצא עליו מתקדש, ויש לשרוף אותו שם.
הקרבן הקבוע שעל המזבח הוא שני כבשים בני שנה, כלומר בתוך שנתם הראשונה, בכל יום תמיד.
את הכבש הראשון מקריבים בבוקר, ואת הכבש השני מקריבים בין הערביים, כלומר אחר הצהריים.
עם הכבש מקריבים מנחה של עשירית האיפה סולת, בלולה בשמן בכמות של רבע ההין, וכן נסך של יין בכמות של רביעית ההין.
את הכבש השני מקריבים בין הערביים עם אותה מנחה של סולת ושמן ועם נסכה כמו בבוקר. שני הקרבנות הם קרבנות עולה הנשרפים לה'.
את עולת התמיד מקריבים בכל הדורות בפתח אוהל מועד, לפני ה'. שם ה' נפגש עם העם, ובמיוחד עם הכוהנים, ושם הוא מדבר עם משה.
אוהל מועד מתקדש בכבודו של ה'. גם לאחר טקסי מילוי ידי הכוהנים וכפרת המזבח, המשכן אינו מתקדש אלא בזכות נוכחות כבוד ה'.
ה' מקדש את אוהל מועד ואת המזבח, וכן את אהרן ואת בניו כדי שיהיו כוהנים לו.
במשכן ובמקדש השכינה נמצאת ומתגלה בתוך עם ישראל, וה' נעשה להם לאלוהים.
בני ישראל יכירו בה' לא רק כמי שהוציא אותם ממצרים בעבר, אלא גם כמי ששוכן בקרבם במשכן באופן קבוע.
ai_explanation_en: This instruction concerns Aaron and his sons, who are to be consecrated to serve as priests. They are to take one bull in its third year and two rams, all of them unblemished.

The basket is to contain various kinds of unleavened wheat-flour baked goods: loaves, cakes mixed with oil, and thin wafers brushed with oil. These are different forms of bread that have not fermented.
All these baked goods are to be placed in one basket and brought together with the bull and the two rams. The specific procedure for each item is explained later.
Aaron and his sons are to be brought to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and immersed or washed in water.
The garments are to be put on Aaron in order: the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate. He is then to be girded with the ephod’s belt.
The turban is to be placed on Aaron’s head, and the holy crown—the frontlet—is to be placed on top of the turban.
The anointing oil is to be poured onto Aaron’s head, before the turban is put on, since the oil is poured on the head rather than on the turban; he is then anointed.
Aaron’s sons are to be brought forward and dressed in tunics.

Aaron and his sons are all to be girded with belts, while the sons are given caps. These acts of dressing and anointing establish not only these priests but their descendants for all generations, appointing Aaron and his sons to the priesthood.
The bull is to be brought before the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons must press their hands firmly on its head, between its horns.
The bull is to be slaughtered before the Lord at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Blood from the bull is to be placed with a finger on each of the four horns of the large altar in the Tabernacle courtyard. The remaining blood in the vessel is to be poured at the base of the altar.

Take all the fat covering the internal organs, the membrane near the liver, and the two kidneys with their surrounding fat. Burn these parts on the altar until they are consumed by smoke; the Sages call them the “ אימורים” (sacrificial portions).

Burn the bull’s flesh, hide, and intestinal waste outside the camp. Although this is an external sin offering whose blood is placed on the outer altar, unlike other such offerings none of its flesh is eaten; everything except the portions burned on the altar is burned outside the camp.
Take the first ram, and have Aaron and his sons place their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram and collect its blood in a vessel. As with burnt offerings, sprinkle it from the vessel onto the corners of the altar so that it reaches all around it, rather than applying it with a finger as in a sin offering.
Cut the ram into its component pieces. Wash its internal parts and legs after removing them, and place them together with the pieces and the head that were cut earlier.
Burn the entire ram on the altar, since a burnt offering is wholly offered to the Lord after its hide is removed and it is cut into pieces. It is a pleasing fragrance and a fire offering to the Lord.
Take the second ram, and have Aaron and his sons place their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram and place some of its blood on the right ear-lobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. The exact meaning of “ear-lobe” is uncertain; the Sages debated whether it refers to the hard part, the soft part, or the middle of the ear, and the remaining blood is sprinkled around the altar.
Take some blood from the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments. In this way, they and their garments are sanctified.

Take from the ram the fat, the fat tail characteristic of many sheep, the fat covering the internal organs, the liver membrane, the kidneys and their fat, and the right thigh. This is the ram of inauguration, the one-time offering for appointing the priests.
Take one loaf from the unleavened bread, one oil-mixed cake, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread before the Lord.
Place all these sacrificial portions and unleavened-bread items in Aaron’s and his sons’ hands. Raise their filled hands as a wave offering before the Lord.

Take the specified portions of the ram and the portion of the bread offering from their hands, and burn them on the altar in addition to the first ram, which was a burnt offering. This is a fire offering to the Lord, producing a pleasing fragrance before Him.
Take the breast of Aaron’s ordination ram and wave it before the Lord. It is to be Moses’ portion; this ram is a peace offering.

Set apart the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the heave offering from the ordination ram. In this ordination offering, the breast was given to Moses and the thigh was burned on the altar, although these portions fundamentally belong to Aaron and his sons; in ordinary peace offerings, both belong to the priests.

From this point onward, the breast and thigh are permanently assigned to Aaron and his sons from the Israelites. They are portions lifted from the Israelites’ peace offerings, which are otherwise given to them for eating; giving these portions to the priests constitutes their offering to the Lord.
Aaron’s sacred garments will pass to his sons after him. Wearing them will elevate them and authorize them for their priestly service.

The son who succeeds Aaron as high priest must wear these garments for seven days before entering the Tent of Meeting to serve in the Sanctuary. This period prepares each future high priest for his service.
Take the ordination ram and boil its flesh in a sacred place, namely, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

Aaron and his sons are to eat the ram’s flesh and the bread remaining in the basket at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Although peace-offering owners normally eat this portion, here the priests are considered its owners and therefore eat it.
The priests are to eat these portions, through which they received atonement and were cleansed and consecrated for their service. No outsider may eat them, because they are holy.

If any of the ram’s flesh or bread remains until morning, it must be burned in fire rather than eaten, because it is holy. The Torah repeats this rule concerning leftover sacrificial meat in several places.
Carry out all these instructions for Aaron and his sons exactly as commanded. Their hands are to be filled and they are to be consecrated for seven days.
Bring the previously mentioned bull as a sin offering each day of the ordination period for atonement. By applying its blood, cleanse the altar, and then anoint it to sanctify it.
For seven days, the altar is to be atoned for and sanctified. From then on it is supremely holy, and any item fit to be offered that touches or is placed on it becomes holy and must be burned there.
The regular offering is two lambs each day, continuously. They must be male lambs still within their first year.
One lamb is to be offered in the morning, and the second between the evenings, meaning in the afternoon.

Each lamb is accompanied by a grain offering: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-quarter of a hin of pressed olive oil, together with a wine libation of one-quarter of a hin. An ephah is a dry measure, and a hin is a liquid measure of about four liters.
The second lamb is offered in the afternoon with the same grain and wine offerings as the morning lamb. Both are burnt offerings, burned as a pleasing fire-offering to God.
This continual burnt offering is to be brought throughout the generations at the Tent of Meeting, where God will meet the people—especially the priests who represent them—and speak with Moses.

God will meet the Israelites there, and the Tabernacle will be sanctified by His glory. Even after the ceremonies installing the priests and atoning for the altar, the Tabernacle becomes holy only through God's glorious presence.
God will sanctify the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and will also sanctify Aaron and his sons so that they can serve as His priests.
God will dwell among the Israelites; in the Tabernacle and later in the Temple, His Presence will be present and revealed among the people, and He will be their God.

The Israelites will know that God is their Lord, who brought them out of Egypt in order to dwell among them. He is not only the One who redeemed them in the past, but also the One who continually resides among them in the Tabernacle.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? In descriptions of sacrifices, the word “tamim” means an animal that is whole and without blemish. This emphasized that the offering was fit for sacred service.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The verse lists three kinds of unleavened baked goods: bread, cakes, and wafers. Some were mixed with oil, while others were brushed with it.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The ephod and the breastpiece were part of the high priest’s special clothing, not ordinary everyday garments. The Hebrew word related to the ephod is connected with fastening or binding.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The expression “fill his hand” is a biblical idiom for appointing and authorizing someone for a role. It does not simply mean filling a hand physically.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? סמיכת הידיים על ראש הבהמה הייתה פעולה סמלית של הזדהות והקדשה לפני הקרבתה.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Placing hands on the animal’s head was a symbolic act of identification and dedication before the sacrifice.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? "קרנות המזבח" היו בליטות בארבע פינות המזבח. הן היו חלק קבוע ממבנהו, ולא קרניים של בעל־חיים.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The “horns of the altar” were projections at its four corners. They were part of the altar’s structure, not the horns of an animal.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? כאשר בשר החטאת נשרף מחוץ למחנה, נוצר הבדל ברור בין מה שנעשה בתוך המרחב המקודש לבין מה שמורחק ממנו.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Burning the sin offering outside the camp created a clear distinction between what took place within the sacred area and what was removed from it.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Blood was placed on the priests’ right ear, hand, and foot. Some interpretations understand this as symbolizing listening, acting, and walking in sacred service.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? In this verse, blood and anointing oil together are connected with consecrating both the person and his clothing. The garments therefore become part of the dedication ceremony.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The sacrifice is called the “ram of ordination” because of its connection to the expression “fill his hand,” meaning to authorize someone for priestly service.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? “Waving” was a ritual act in which an offering was lifted or moved before God. The word does not necessarily describe one specific motion.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Portions of certain sacrifices were given to the priests. In this way, the priests’ service was supported through offerings brought by the Israelites.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? שבעת הימים של לבישת בגדי הקודש יוצרים תקופת הכשרה והקדשה לפני תחילת השירות של הכוהן החדש.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The seven days of wearing the sacred garments create a period of preparation and consecration before a new priest begins his service.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? המילה "תמיד" כאן מתארת קורבן קבוע וחוזר מדי יום, ולא קורבן שמוקרב ברציפות בכל רגע.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Here, the word “tamid” describes a regular sacrifice repeated every day, not one offered continuously every moment.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? אוהל מועד נקרא כך מפני שהוא המקום שבו ה' נועד, כלומר נפגש או מתקשר, עם בני ישראל.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The Tent of Meeting is called by that name because it is the place where God meets or communicates with the Israelites.
